title: Compass and Landfall
premise: Mirabel Sterling has spent two decades running survey lines across three continents, outrunning the memory of her archaeologist father's final, disastrous expedition into the Karagol Range. When her father's old rival, Elias Vane, hires her crew to recover a lost survey cache before the first snows seal the passes, she discovers the job is bait: Vane wants the cache because it holds her father's field notes — and proof that Mirabel was the one who found the site that killed him. Crossing the range with Vane's son Tomas, whose loyalties split between his father and the woman he is coming to love, Mirabel must decide whether identity is inherited or chosen. At the summit pass, she chooses neither vengeance nor erasure: she publishes the notes under both names, forgives the dead, and claims the crew that carried her through as her true family.
about_author: Lior Reyes is a former trail-crew cook turned novelist who writes adventure stories about people who measure their lives in miles. They live in a converted survey station in the northern Rockies with two stubborn dogs and an unreliable woodstove.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On a desert survey in Utah, Mirabel runs her crew with clockwork precision and refuses a birthday cake, revealing her habit of counting distance instead of time. A telegram arrives from Elias Vane offering a contract for 'the Karagol job.' She burns it. Emotional beat: the armor of routine cracking at its first seam.

chapters.title: The Rival's Letter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Vane's second letter includes a page of her father's handwriting — unmistakable, damning, intimate. Her crew, led by loyal foreman Odile, votes to take the job over her objection; they need the winter wages. Mirabel agrees, telling herself it's only business. Emotional beat: dread disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Tomas Vane's POV. Tomas meets the Sterling crew at the mountain railhead, carrying his father's sealed orders he hasn't read. He sizes up Mirabel as the legend he grew up hearing about — brilliant, cold, cursed. First friction over route choice. Emotional beat: wary respect mistaken for dislike.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Around the fire, Odile reveals she was on the original Karagol expedition twenty years ago; she knows what the cache holds and why Mirabel's father never came down. Mirabel learns Vane has told her crew nothing. Betrayal simmers. Emotional beat: the past arriving faster than the mules.

chapters.title: The Low Road
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The combined crews enter the range by the river gorge. Tomas reads his father's orders at last: retrieve the cache, burn anything else, tell no one what the notes contain. He hesitates over the last instruction. Emotional beat: the first crack in filial duty.

chapters.title: Riverbend
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A flash flood nearly takes the supply train; Mirabel and Tomas save each other's people, working in wordless sync. That night she catches him burning a page and demands the truth; he gives her half of it. Emotional beat: trust built in water and almost drowned in ash.

chapters.title: The Map Her Father Drew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The route matches a hand-drawn map sewn into Mirabel's old jacket lining — her father's work, made for her when she was twelve. She realizes Vane hired her not despite who she is but because of it. Emotional beat: being seen as a key, not a person.

chapters.title: Treeline
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Above treeline, weather turns early. An argument over pushing on versus sheltering splits the crews; Odile backs Mirabel, and Tomas sides against his own father's timetable for the first time openly. Emotional beat: choosing a side without admitting which side it is.

chapters.title: Snowlight
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Stormbound in a cave, the crews trade stories; Mirabel, cornered by kindness, tells the truth of the night her father died — that she found the site first, that he took credit, that the fall happened arguing over it. The cave goes quiet. Emotional beat: confession as avalanche.

chapters.title: Vane's Version
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas confronts his father by letter via runner, demanding the whole story. Vane's reply admits he provoked the quarrel that killed Mirabel's father — rivalry sharpened into sabotage — and that the notes prove it. He orders Tomas to keep her from reading them. Emotional beat: inheritance curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Cache Coordinates
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Clear skies, hard climbing. Mirabel deciphers her father's map fully and realizes the cache isn't where Vane thinks — her father moved it, leaving a riddle only she could solve. She says nothing to Vane's party. Emotional beat: power shifting quietly into her hands.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Frostbite takes two mules and nearly a man; Mirabel amputates frost-dead fingers by lantern light without flinching. Tomas watches her lead and understands his father hired the wrong Sterling — or exactly the right one. Emotional beat: love arriving as admiration before it has a name.

chapters.title: The Pass Below the Snows
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They reach the cache cairn ahead of schedule. Inside: her father's notes, Vane's original expedition ledger, and a letter addressed to Mirabel, written the week he died. She reads none of them yet, hands shaking. Emotional beat: grief postponed one more ridge.

chapters.title: What the Notes Say
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Vane's advance party arrives by the high route, earlier than any reckoning allowed. Vane demands the cache; Mirabel refuses to hand over the letter. Standoff on the ice. Tomas steps between them. Emotional beat: duty and love finally facing each other across a rope's width.

chapters.title: Crevasse
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The standoff breaks when the snowbridge fails; Vane falls into a crevasse and Mirabel — the daughter of the man he ruined — leads the rescue that saves him. In the rope-work she finds her answer about who she is. Emotional beat: mercy as the hardest climb.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Frost-bound and out of options, Mirabel finally reads her father's letter: he knew he'd taken credit from her, he wrote it down so the record would someday correct itself, and he asked her forgiveness — not the mountain's. Emotional beat: the weight of twenty years set down.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The storm everyone feared arrives with them still above the pass. Retreat is impossible; the only line down is her father's untested route from the map. Vane, broken and humbled, defers to Mirabel's judgment. Emotional beat: leadership accepted like a burden willingly shouldered.

chapters.title: Her Father's Route
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The descent through the icefall, following instructions written for a twelve-year-old. Every anchor holds because her father was, in the end, the better surveyor — and she is better still. They lose supplies, not lives. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the dead through competence and care.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The crews reach the valley as the passes close behind them. Vane, half-frozen and honest at last, offers Mirabel sole authorship of everything. She refuses the frame: the notes will be published under both names, his errors included. Emotional beat: justice chosen over victory.

chapters.title: Names on the Page
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Weeks later, in a lowland town, the manuscript goes to the printer with both Sterlings' names and Vane's confession appended. Tomas asks Mirabel what she'll do next season; she says she hasn't decided, and for the first time that feels like freedom rather than flight. Emotional beat: love spoken sideways, then plainly.

chapters.title: The Crew That Carried Her
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Winter quarters: Odile, the injured climber, the muleteers, Tomas — the found family gathered under one roof, arguing happily about next year's contracts. Mirabel lets them celebrate her birthday, twenty years late and right on time. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Compass True
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Spring. On the ridge above town, Mirabel buries her father's compass at the head of the new trail she's surveyed herself — not to forget him, but to stop navigating by him. She turns south toward the next range with her crew beside her. Emotional beat: identity claimed; the road open.
